newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Brokers say activity on Palestinian bourse rising.
newsitem.headline: Brokers say activity on Palestinian bourse rising.

text.p: Brokers said trading activity in the nascent Palestinian stock exchange increased during the third weekly day of trading on Tuesday.
Safwan Bataina, general manager of the Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE), said the exchange would not publish any statistics until the trade volume reached meaningful levels.
But brokers said there was an increase in the number of shares offered for trading and the size of orders placed by investors during Tuesday's session.
"Trading is still in early stages but the number of shares offered for trading is increasing," one broker said.

He said that while most single orders were below 1,000 shares during the first week of trading, some orders reached more than 1,500 shares this week. He said that indicated confidence in the Palestinian companies listed on the exchange.
"In every trading session, there are more companies whose shares are being traded. All the signs point to a healthy start," he said.

Bataina had said 23 companies were listed on the bourse when it was launched last month and that 22 others were in the process of joining. Four brokerage houses have been acredited and a fifth is awaiting approval.

The PSE has been holding one trading session a week during its running-in phase, which Bataina said would last for several weeks. Regular trading, with several sessions per week, would begin as trading volume builds up, he said.

The market was set up to help attract long-term investment from expatriate Palestinians, foreign capital and provide an alternative to common forms of investments such as bank deposits and real estate.
